reason: The count is right (LDY #4 loop 2+8+11=21 cycles, LDY #2 loop 2+4+5=11: 10 a call, 0 bytes, no page crossing), but this is hardware-timed code the project deliberately keeps as the MOS writes it: sfx50.6502's header says the chip is written 'as the MOS writes it ... with the MOS's delays' and sfx_write cites MOS 3.20 &F5E6, whose LDY #4 post-high wait this copies (decision 25's driver, reusable). Shortening it changes the SN76489 write-enable/port-A timing, which jsbeeb cannot model, so no proof in the gate can show the sound is unchanged on a real machine (rule 1: same sound; 'measure, do not recall'): the candidate's own relies_on concedes 'hardware timing the emulator cannot show'. Its >=31-cycle argument covers only the driver's own next chip write; it does not cover the VIA traffic that follows sfx_silence in give_irq_back (PLP, RTS, CLI, then the MOS's interrupt, its 100 Hz tick and keyboard scan drive port A with DDRA changed and its own OSWORD 7 sound writes) or what follows the vsync handler's RTI (keydown_int writes port A/ORB from the main loop), where the gap from WE high to the next port A write shrinks from 27+ to 17+ cycles. Whether the chip needs that tail is not established here; a deviation from the MOS's write timing would need an agreed decision and a real-hardware check (beeb-cross-emulator), not a grind batch. Unsure, so refuted.
